newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent hits skids as mid-June cargoes struggle.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent hits skids as mid-June cargoes struggle.

text.p: Dated Brent was on the skids again on Wednesday as cargoes of the benchmark grade found exits from the sloppy North Sea blocked by weak U.S. markets, traders said.
A very prompt June 10-12 Brent cargo was sold by a European major to a refiner for July Brent -48 cents a barrel, four cents cheaper than the lowest deal reported on Tuesday.
Bearish U.S. inventory data was making transatlantic sales extremely difficult.
"Margins aren't great, WTI (NYMEX crude) has fallen out of bed and it looks as if Dated (Brent) is trying to find an arbitrage, find support," said a trader.
American Petroleum Institute (API) figures released late on Tuesday showed U.S. crude stocks rose by 8.4 million barrels last week despite record gasoline production.
The prospect of a swift resumption of Iraqi exports under the U.N. oil-for-food deal was adding to the bearish sentiment, traders said.
"Everything's a bit weaker this morning because of the stocks figures and the fact that the renewal of the Iraqi deal may be faster than expected," said a trader.
Cash Brent spreads slipped, July/August losing two cents to trade at -18 cents. July Brent shed 11 cents to $18.79 a barrel.
Only one June 19-21 Brent cargo was expected to turn wet on Wednesday but traders said there were still plenty of cargoes with earlier loading dates available.
Other North Sea crudes were starting to slip in the wake of Dated's slide in the last 10 days as details emerged of deals on Tuesday which pointed to softer differentials.

A Statfjord cargo loading June 24-26 traded at Dated Brent +25 cents, three cents weaker than another deal on Tuesday. There was also unconfirmed talk of a Forties deal at +25 cents, some 10 cents weaker than the last reported trade.
